subject: Urgent: HealthSpire 5xx/429 surge, retry amplification — immediate action & exec notification
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan@healthspire.com>, procurement@healthspire.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HealthSpire: sudden 5xx/429 spike — need immediate sync

Hi Ethan / HealthSpire team,

We just observed a sharp increase in error responses from your production traffic routed to your dedicated pool (us-west-2-dedicated-3). Key metrics in the last 18 minutes:
- Overall request failure (5xx/429) ~18% (baseline <1%)
- 5xx specifically ~12%
- p95 latency up from ~120ms to ~2.4s for text-generation routes
- Significant increase in client-side timeouts and retry attempts, producing what looks like retry amplification.

I've attached a short error log snippet and flagged this to our SRE team. Initial triage points we see: GPU node saturation in your dedicated pool, autoscaling lag on adding new nodes, and long-running requests (large sequence lengths) holding KV caches. Ops is prioritizing this but I want to get an immediate alignment on two things:
1) Can HealthSpire accept a short ~30 min failover to our hosted fallback model (lower cost but more elastic) while we stabilize the dedicated pool?
2) Can we schedule a 15-min call now to confirm mitigation and customer impact (timeouts, DPA concerns, SLA)?

Next steps from Redwood: I'm asking SRE to open a scale-up and patch autoscaler aggressive thresholds, and to deploy a temporary routing rule to shift a portion of traffic away from the saturated nodes. Lauren is on standby.

Attaching: healthspire-error-log-20270630.txt

Connor O'Brien

Subject: Re: HealthSpire: sudden 5xx/429 spike — need immediate sync

Connor — thanks for the quick heads up. We're seeing a material impact to patient-facing flows (forms failing intermittently). Two asks from our side:
1) ETA for a mitigation that reduces errors to <2%; we need a timeline for exec updates.
2) Given this impacted production, we will need a proposal for credits or SLA exceptions — I can route to procurement once we have a scope.

We can join a 15-min call now.

—Ethan
VP Product, HealthSpire
ethan@healthspire.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Ethan Cole <ethan@healthspire.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthSpire: sudden 5xx/429 spike — need immediate sync

Ethan / Connor — quick triage update from infra:
- Root cause (probable): workload spike with unusually long sequence lengths and a few large batched requests holding KV cache and saturating 3 nodes in the dedicated pool.
- Symptom: autoscaler didn't provision fast enough because target_utilization threshold was conservative; queued requests timed out and triggered client retries (amplified the load).

Immediate mitigations we are applying (ETA 20–40m):
- Force-scale: add 4 ephemeral GPU nodes to us-west-2-dedicated-3 (already requested; PD-INC-9821 opened).
- Temporary routing: divert 30% of incoming traffic for your tenant to the hosted fallback model (elastic, different instance family) to absorb spikes.
- Short-term config: lower request timeout at the proxy (from 15s to 10s) and enforce a client-side max_retries=1 recommendation for 1 hour to prevent retry loops.

Operational asks for HealthSpire:
- If possible, suspend any large batch inference jobs for 1 hour (we see a couple of high-TTL jobs from IPs tied to your integration).
- Share any recent deployment or traffic shift that started around 08:50 PDT.

I'll monitor the scale-up and post updates here. If escalation to execs is needed, Connor, suggest looping in Marissa for account-level comms.

—Lauren
Sr Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Ethan Cole <ethan@healthspire.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, procurement@healthspire.com
Date: 2027-06-30T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: HealthSpire: sudden 5xx/429 spike — immediate action & exec notification

Marissa / Sean — forwarding the thread. We're executing Lauren's immediate mitigations (scale-up + partial routing). HealthSpire is asking for a credit estimate and ETA for stabilization.

Quick context for execs: this is a production-affecting incident tied to capacity exhaustion and autoscale lag on a Dedicated pool. HealthSpire is a mid-enterprise account with active renewal discussions (deal D-3491). I recommend we:
- Prioritize the scale-up and routing now (Lauren has steps).
- Prep a one-page incident summary and credit proposal for Ethan (I can draft with CS).
- Consider short-term capacity commitment for this customer if they accept (reserved nodes) to prevent recurrence.

Connor
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ethan Cole <ethan@healthspire.com>
Cc: procurement@healthspire.com
Date: 2027-06-30T13:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HealthSpire: sudden 5xx/429 spike — immediate action & exec notification

Team / Ethan — operational update (PD-INC-9821):
- We forced +4 nodes into the dedicated pool at 13:12 PDT; observed a steady drop in queue depth and a 5xx rate reduction target: within 25 minutes error rate fell from 12% to ~3%.
- Deployed a temporary autoscaler patch to lower target_utilization and shorten evaluation_window to 30s — should reduce lag on ramp-ups.
- Identified a heavy client pattern: a batch job that sends long-sequence requests every ~10m; we'll throttle/limit such jobs by tenant in the short term.

Next steps (24–72h):
- Post-mortem and incident summary (root cause analysis + timeline).
- Recommend reserved capacity or guaranteed burst pool for HealthSpire; will provide cost delta.
- Work with product to harden autoscaler heuristics and to provide tenant-level QoS (per-tenant request caps, early rejection for oversized sequences).

PD incident id: PD-INC-9821
Tracking link: https://pagerduty.redwood.ai/incidents/PD-INC-9821

—Sean
Head of SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan@healthspire.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, procurement@healthspire.com
Date: 2027-07-01T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: HealthSpire incident update & next steps

Ethan / team — following up after yesterday's mitigation:
- Current status: 5xx/429 now holding ~1.5% over last hour, latency back near baseline for most routes.
- Actions completed: forced scale-up (+4 nodes), temporary routing to hosted fallback, autoscaler patch deployed, tenant throttling for oversized batch jobs.
- Attached: mutual action plan (healthspire-mutual-action-plan.xlsx) with next steps for a formal post-incident review, credit proposal, and optional reserved capacity pricing.

Proposed customer-facing timeline:
1) Today: incident summary + immediate credits proposal (Connor + Marissa).
2) 48h: joint post-mortem with SRE and HealthSpire engineers.
3) 7d: decision on reserved capacity or burst SLA and config changes to prevent retry amplification.

Please confirm acceptance of the MAP and whether procurement wants us to draft a formal credit note. Happy to jump on a call if you'd prefer.

Thanks for patience — we'll pull the full RCA and cost assessment for next steps.

Connor O'Brien
